items.name: Class
items.summary: The high-level intermediate representation of a character class.

methods.name: case_fold_simple
methods.summary: Apply Unicode simple case folding to this character class, in place. The character class will be expanded to include all simple case folded character variants.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this character class is empty. That is, it has no elements.

methods.name: is_utf8
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this character class will only ever match valid UTF-8.

methods.name: literal
methods.summary: If this class consists of exactly one element (whether a codepoint or a byte), then return it as a literal byte string.

methods.name: maximum_len
methods.summary: Returns the length, in bytes, of the longest string matched by this character class.

methods.name: minimum_len
methods.summary: Returns the length, in bytes, of the smallest string matched by this character class.

methods.name: negate
methods.summary: Negate this character class in place.

methods.name: try_case_fold_simple
methods.summary: Apply Unicode simple case folding to this character class, in place. The character class will be expanded to include all simple case folded character variants.

items.name: Dot
items.summary: A type describing the different flavors of `.`.

items.name: ErrorKind
items.summary: The type of an error that occurred while building an `Hir`.

items.name: HirKind
items.summary: The underlying kind of an arbitrary [`Hir`] expression.

methods.name: subs
methods.summary: Returns a slice of this kind's sub-expressions, if any.

items.name: Look
items.summary: The high-level intermediate representation for a look-around assertion.

methods.name: as_char
methods.summary: Returns a convenient single codepoint representation of this look-around assertion. Each assertion is guaranteed to be represented by a distinct character.

methods.name: as_repr
methods.summary: Return the underlying representation of this look-around enumeration as an integer. Giving the return value to the [`Look::from_repr`] constructor is guaranteed to return the same look-around variant that one started with within a semver c…

methods.name: from_repr
methods.summary: Given the underlying representation of a `Look` value, return the corresponding `Look` value if the representation is valid. Otherwise `None` is returned.

methods.name: reversed
methods.summary: Flip the look-around assertion to its equivalent for reverse searches. For example, `StartLF` gets translated to `EndLF`.

items.name: Capture
items.summary: The high-level intermediate representation for a capturing group.

items.name: ClassBytes
items.summary: A set of characters represented by arbitrary bytes.

methods.name: case_fold_simple
methods.summary: Expand this character class such that it contains all case folded characters. For example, if this class consists of the range `a-z`, then applying case folding will result in the class containing both the ranges `a-z` and `A-Z`.

methods.name: difference
methods.summary: Subtract the given byte class from this byte class, in place.

methods.name: empty
methods.summary: Create a new class with no ranges.

methods.name: intersect
methods.summary: Intersect this byte class with the given byte class, in place.

methods.name: is_ascii
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this character class will either match nothing or only ASCII bytes. Stated differently, this returns false if and only if this class contains a non-ASCII byte.

methods.name: iter
methods.summary: Return an iterator over all ranges in this class.

methods.name: literal
methods.summary: If this class consists of exactly one byte, then return it as a literal byte string.

methods.name: maximum_len
methods.summary: Returns the length, in bytes, of the longest string matched by this character class.

methods.name: minimum_len
methods.summary: Returns the length, in bytes, of the smallest string matched by this character class.

methods.name: negate
methods.summary: Negate this byte class.

methods.name: new
methods.signature: fn new<I>(ranges: I) -> ClassBytes where I: IntoIterator<Item = ClassBytesRange>
methods.summary: Create a new class from a sequence of ranges.

methods.name: push
methods.summary: Add a new range to this set.

methods.name: ranges
methods.summary: Return the underlying ranges as a slice.

methods.name: symmetric_difference
methods.summary: Compute the symmetric difference of the given byte classes, in place.

methods.name: to_unicode_class
methods.summary: If this class consists of only ASCII ranges, then return its corresponding and equivalent Unicode class.

methods.name: union
methods.summary: Union this byte class with the given byte class, in place.

items.name: ClassBytesIter

methods.name: end

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the number of bytes in this range.

methods.name: start
methods.summary: Return the start of this range.

methods.name: iter

methods.name: literal

items.name: Error
items.summary: An error that can occur while translating an `Ast` to a `Hir`.

methods.name: kind
methods.summary: Return the type of this error.

methods.name: pattern
methods.summary: The original pattern string in which this error occurred.

methods.name: span
methods.summary: Return the span at which this error occurred.

items.name: Hir
items.summary: A high-level intermediate representation (HIR) for a regular expression.

methods.name: alternation
methods.summary: Returns the alternation of the given expressions.

methods.name: capture
methods.summary: Creates a capture HIR expression.

methods.name: class
methods.summary: Creates a class HIR expression. The class may either be defined over ranges of Unicode codepoints or ranges of raw byte values.

methods.name: concat
methods.summary: Returns the concatenation of the given expressions.

methods.name: dot
methods.summary: Returns an HIR expression for `.`.

methods.name: empty
methods.summary: Returns an empty HIR expression.

methods.name: fail
methods.summary: Returns an HIR expression that can never match anything. That is, the size of the set of strings in the language described by the HIR returned is `0`.

methods.name: into_kind
methods.summary: Consumes ownership of this HIR expression and returns its underlying `HirKind`.

methods.name: kind
methods.summary: Returns a reference to the underlying HIR kind.

methods.name: literal
methods.summary: Creates a literal HIR expression.

methods.name: look
methods.summary: Creates a look-around assertion HIR expression.

methods.name: properties
methods.summary: Returns the properties computed for this `Hir`.

methods.name: repetition
methods.summary: Creates a repetition HIR expression.

items.name: Literal
items.summary: The high-level intermediate representation of a literal.

methods.name: contains
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the given look-around assertion is in this set.

methods.name: contains_anchor
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set contains any anchor assertions. This includes both "start/end of haystack" and "start/end of line."

methods.name: contains_anchor_crlf
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set contains any "start/end of line" anchors that are CRLF-aware. This doesn't include "start/end of haystack" or "start/end of line-feed" anchors.

methods.name: contains_anchor_haystack
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set contains any "start/end of haystack" anchors. This doesn't include "start/end of line" anchors.

methods.name: contains_anchor_lf
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set contains any "start/end of line" anchors that only treat `\n` as line terminators. This does not include haystack anchors or CRLF aware line anchors.

methods.name: contains_anchor_line
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set contains any "start/end of line" anchors. This doesn't include "start/end of haystack" anchors. This includes both `\n` line anchors and CRLF (`\r\n`) aware line anchors.

methods.name: contains_word
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set contains any word boundary or negated word boundary assertions. This include both Unicode and ASCII word boundaries.

methods.name: contains_word_ascii
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set contains any ASCII word boundary or negated ASCII word boundary assertions.

methods.name: contains_word_unicode
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set contains any Unicode word boundary or negated Unicode word boundary assertions.

methods.name: empty
methods.summary: Create an empty set of look-around assertions.

methods.name: full
methods.summary: Create a full set of look-around assertions.

methods.name: insert
methods.summary: Return a new set that is equivalent to the original, but with the given assertion added to it. If the assertion is already in the set, then the returned set is equivalent to the original.

methods.name: intersect
methods.summary: Returns a new set that is the intersection of this and the one given.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this set is empty.

methods.name: iter
methods.summary: Returns an iterator over all of the look-around assertions in this set.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of look-around assertions in this set.

methods.name: read_repr
methods.summary: Return a `LookSet` from the slice given as a native endian 32-bit integer.

methods.name: remove
methods.summary: Return a new set that is equivalent to the original, but with the given assertion removed from it. If the assertion is not in the set, then the returned set is equivalent to the original.

methods.name: set_insert
methods.summary: Updates this set in place with the result of inserting the given assertion into this set.

methods.name: set_intersect
methods.summary: Updates this set in place with the result of intersecting it with the one given.

methods.name: set_remove
methods.summary: Updates this set in place with the result of removing the given assertion from this set.

methods.name: set_subtract
methods.summary: Updates this set in place with the result of subtracting the given set from this set.

methods.name: set_union
methods.summary: Updates this set in place with the result of unioning it with the one given.

methods.name: singleton
methods.summary: Create a look-around set containing the look-around assertion given.

methods.name: subtract
methods.summary: Returns a new set that is the result of subtracting the given set from this set.

methods.name: union
methods.summary: Returns a new set that is the union of this and the one given.

methods.name: write_repr
methods.summary: Write a `LookSet` as a native endian 32-bit integer to the beginning of the slice given.

items.name: LookSetIter
items.summary: An iterator over all look-around assertions in a [`LookSet`].

items.name: Properties
items.summary: A type that collects various properties of an HIR value.

methods.name: explicit_captures_len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of explicit capturing groups in the corresponding HIR.

methods.name: is_alternation_literal
methods.summary: Return true if and only if this HIR is either a simple literal or an alternation of simple literals. This is only true when this HIR expression is either itself a `Literal` or a concatenation of only `Literal`s or an alternation of only `L…

methods.name: is_literal
methods.summary: Return true if and only if this HIR is a simple literal. This is only true when this HIR expression is either itself a `Literal` or a concatenation of only `Literal`s.

methods.name: is_utf8
methods.summary: Return true if and only if the corresponding HIR will always match valid UTF-8.

methods.name: look_set
methods.summary: Returns a set of all look-around assertions that appear at least once in this HIR value.

methods.name: look_set_prefix
methods.summary: Returns a set of all look-around assertions that appear as a prefix for this HIR value. That is, the set returned corresponds to the set of assertions that must be passed before matching any bytes in a haystack.

methods.name: look_set_prefix_any
methods.summary: Returns a set of all look-around assertions that appear as a _possible_ prefix for this HIR value. That is, the set returned corresponds to the set of assertions that _may_ be passed before matching any bytes in a haystack.

methods.name: look_set_suffix
methods.summary: Returns a set of all look-around assertions that appear as a suffix for this HIR value. That is, the set returned corresponds to the set of assertions that must be passed in order to be considered a match after all other consuming HIR expr…

methods.name: look_set_suffix_any
methods.summary: Returns a set of all look-around assertions that appear as a _possible_ suffix for this HIR value. That is, the set returned corresponds to the set of assertions that _may_ be passed before matching any bytes in a haystack.

methods.name: maximum_len
methods.summary: Returns the length (in bytes) of the longest string matched by this HIR.

methods.name: memory_usage
methods.summary: Returns the total amount of heap memory usage, in bytes, used by this `Properties` value.

methods.name: minimum_len
methods.summary: Returns the length (in bytes) of the smallest string matched by this HIR.

methods.name: static_explicit_captures_len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of explicit capturing groups that appear in every possible match.

methods.name: union
methods.signature: fn union<I, P>(props: I) -> Properties where I: IntoIterator<Item = P>, P: core::borrow::Borrow<Properties>
methods.summary: Returns a new set of properties that corresponds to the union of the iterator of properties given.

items.name: Repetition
items.summary: The high-level intermediate representation of a repetition operator.

methods.name: with
methods.summary: Returns a new repetition with the same `min`, `max` and `greedy` values, but with its sub-expression replaced with the one given.
